chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Baqqah, from Al-Hasan Al-Siqqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the fasting person who wears a wet garment, he said: 'No' (it is disliked), and he should not smell the basil.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a fasting person smelling basil or wearing wet clothes?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the rulings on wearing wet garments and smelling basil during fasting, reflecting the scholarly debate between *makruh* (disliked) and *haram* (prohibited) depending on the degree of absorption. The mention of *al-Siqal* (the potter) highlights the transmission chain through trusted companions, while the specific inclusion of basil (*rayhan*) points to the sensory experiences considered in classical fiqh. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving the spiritual purity and physical comfort of the fasting state, distinguishing between minor distractions and acts that nullify the fast.
